caption: : Avg. performance across 11 datasets (y-axis) consistently improves as the number of training examples increases (x-axis). Max is 29k examples, the full size of our dataset.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between the number of training datasets and average performance. The x-axis represents the "# of training dataset (k)" with a linear scale, ranging from 5 to 30 in intervals of 5, representing thousands of datasets. The y-axis represents "Average Performance" with a linear scale, ranging from 48 to 56 in intervals of 2, with no units specified. A single black line with circular markers and a solid style is plotted, showing an increase in average performance as the number of training datasets increases, starting at approximately 48 at 5k datasets and rising to around 56 at 30k datasets, with notable values at 10k (around 50.5) and 20k (around 53).
